The expression \"Llegó Pacheco\" (Pachec:
The expression "Llegó Pacheco" (Pacheco arrived) originated in Venezuela and it is used to refer to the arrival of "cold" weather, specifically in December and in the city of Caracas.

The legend tells that a flower farmer named Antonio Pacheco came down to Caracas from Galipán, a small town on the El Ávila hill, at the end of November or beginning of December to sell his flowers.

His arrival coincided with the onset of cold season, which is why he began to be associated with this time of year. Pacheco came down three times a week, accompanied by his donkeys and the load of flowers. He sold them in front of the La Pastora church and then went to the San José Flower Market.

This tradition has been maintained for many years and became a part of Venezuelan folklore. Nowadays "Llegó Pacheco" is still used to refer to the cold and the arrival of Christmas.

It is common in Caracas to hear phrases like "Esta haciendo Pacheco" (It's getting cold) or "El Pacheco está fuerte este año." (This year the cold is strong)
